insight.title: Your Body Is Constantly Glowing in the Dark
insight.subtitle: The invisible light your cells are emitting right now.
insight.notificationHook: Your body is constantly glowing in the dark

sections.text: Your body is constantly emitting light. Right now, you are literally glowing in the dark, but the light is just too faint for your own eyes to see.
This is living light. Chemical reactions inside your cells constantly leak tiny packets of light, which peak in the late afternoon when your body is working the hardest.
Ultra-sensitive cameras can easily capture this, mapping bright patches across your face. You are constantly walking around in a cloud of your own light.
Your body is making light you will never see.

candidatePool.title: The fine print in insurance policy nobody reads until it matters
candidatePool.description: Policies that appear similar can define illnesses, treatments and payout triggers very differently.
candidatePool.why: Your medical or emergency claims may be unexpectedly denied.
candidatePool.context: Discrepancies in insurance contract definitions are leading to unexpected coverage gaps for many policyholders.
candidatePool.next: Consumers may increasingly demand clearer, standardized policy language from insurers.

candidatePool.title: In Nepal’s highlands, climate change threatens Tibet’s Bon faith

candidatePool.why: Unique cultural legacies and local livelihoods face permanent loss.
candidatePool.context: Climate-induced flooding is destroying heritage sites and homes in remote Nepalese villages.

candidatePool.bigger: Climate change is actively erasing cultural history in isolated communities.

candidatePool.title: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's record-low economic approval rating

candidatePool.why: Public perception of the economy can influence your personal financial confidence.
candidatePool.context: Political analysts debated the implications of historically low economic approval ratings for the current administration.
candidatePool.next: Policy shifts may occur as the administration seeks to boost approval.
candidatePool.bigger: Domestic economic sentiment remains a primary driver of political outcomes.

candidatePool.title: As ILO convention turns 30, India’s home-based workers demand equal rights
candidatePool.description: Convention 177 was adopted on 20 June 1996, recognising home-based workers on a par with traditional wage earners.
candidatePool.why: Workers may soon gain better legal protections and standard benefits.
candidatePool.context: Advocates are pushing for formal recognition and equal rights for India’s massive home-based workforce.
candidatePool.next: National labor laws may be amended to include these informal workers.
candidatePool.bigger: The global shift toward flexible work requires modernizing outdated labor protections.

candidatePool.title: Utah marks a year of battling measles, with no clear end in sight
candidatePool.description: More than 680 people have gotten sick since the state's first outbreak began on June 20, 2025.
candidatePool.why: Healthcare resources in the region remain under significant, prolonged strain.
candidatePool.context: A measles outbreak in Utah has persisted for a full year with hundreds of reported cases.
candidatePool.next: Public health officials may implement stricter vaccination requirements for schools.
candidatePool.bigger: Vaccine-preventable diseases are seeing a resurgence due to shifting health trends.
